author: @tibortoth277
text:
When you completely shake up a winning team, it will never work the same way as the previous one. When Szoboszlai and Mac Allister arrived at the club, Klopp’s team was not playing in the Champions League. However, the new players managed to integrate into the squad quickly and, although they didn’t win the league title (even though they came close), they did win the FA Cup. That already showed that a strong team was forming.

In the following season they even won the league with Slot (a new manager). The title wasn’t really about the coach – it was because by then the team had already developed strong chemistry.

Then came the bad decision from the club’s leadership: they completely dismantled the championship-winning team. As a result, the team dropped back to the level of the 2022/23 season, when it wasn’t yet ready to win trophies.

So it’s not the coach’s fault that they are where they are now. The reality is that a new team has been built with new players, and they still need time to develop chemistry.

Unfortunately, this season will likely be about building that cohesion, and there will probably be more changes in the summer as well. You should never make such massive changes to a team, because it simply won’t work. They could spend all the money in the world and it still wouldn’t fix that.

author: @navaneethkrishnan5401
text:
Bro I have genuinely seen enough. I have reached levels of football-induced psychosis previously thought impossible. I wake up in cold sweats whispering “verticality” and “positional rotations” like they’re going to save us. THEY ARE NOT SAVING US.

Arne Slot has Liverpool playing like someone opened Football Manager, clicked “gegenpress,” and then immediately went afk to make a sandwich.

Every week it’s the same script:

• 73% possession • 812 passes between center-backs • One (1) shot directly at the goalkeeper’s chest • Me staring at the wall contemplating existence

Why are we playing 4D chess when checkers would do??? Why is our buildup slower than Windows 98 on dial-up??? I have watched glaciers move with more urgency than our transition play.

The midfield? Vibes. The defense? Interpretive dance. The attack? A polite suggestion.

And don’t even get me started on the substitutions. It’s like he spins a wheel labeled “confuse everyone” and just commits to whatever it lands on. 85th minute and we’re down? Perfect time to make a like-for-like swap that changes absolutely nothing. Tactical masterclass.

I was promised intensity. I was promised evolution. I was promised a brave new era. Instead I am watching 90 minutes of controlled breathing exercises with a scoreboard.

At this point I’d accept chaotic hoofball. I’d accept three red cards and a 5–4 loss. I’d accept literally any emotion other than this sterile laboratory football where we dominate xG in theory and dominate absolutely nothing in reality.

I am tired. My ancestors did not survive plagues and industrial revolutions for me to witness a backpass compilation every weekend.

Slotball has me googling “how to become emotionally detached from sports” at 2am.

Anyway see you next matchday.

author: @NativeWorldTV
text:
Slot should be sacked because Liverpool have fallen below the minimum standard expected of a title-level club. After 34 league games, Liverpool are 4th, with 17 wins, 13 losses and 58 points, tied with Aston Villa, and their Champions League place is still not secure.

The biggest issue is not just the league position — it is the pattern of collapse. Liverpool have reportedly lost 11 Premier League games under Slot this season, and the latest 3-2 defeat to Manchester United showed the same flaws again: slow start, poor defensive control, chasing the game, then conceding again after getting back level. We didn’t fight back into game as much United just imploded on themselves.

A Liverpool manager can survive a bad season if there is clear progress, but this looks like regression. They are out of the EFL Cup early, reached only the FA Cup quarter-finals, and the Champions League quarter-finals, while sitting 4th domestically despite having a squad expected to challenge.

Elite managers do not repeatedly allow their team to start matches like they are surprised by the opponent. The standard has to be ruthless: Liverpool are not Spurs. They are not a “top-four is enough” club. If you have 13 league defeats by early May, uncertainty over Champions League qualification, and no serious trophy momentum, the manager has failed the Liverpool benchmark.

The final reason: keeping him risks normalising decline. Once Liverpool accept “nearly top four” after being champions-level, the club becomes softer. The argument is simple:

17 wins and 13 losses is not a project. It is a warning sign.

author: @YNWABorder
text: Even in corporate companies they bring in someone with the same level of seniority to the outgoing person. Example if a finance director is leaving then they will replace that position with another proven finance director who has the experience to ensure business is not interrupted. I’m just baffled how a head coach could have been selected to replace a manager. It’s like appointing a kitchen helper to become the head chef, the reason people become manager is after learning about how to manage a team and then they prove themselves and then only get the job they deserve. Guess Liverpool management just wanted a person who will be able to take the blame and put on a poker face and not question the managements decisions. This was how we were playing under Brendan Rodgers and sitting almost in the same position in the table and about the same time when he was sacked and Klopp came in. But rest assured fellow Liverpool fans Slot will still be here even after we are relegated because he is untouchable for winning us the league last season. Some People will say we are over reacting but just look at our position we are in mid table and if we stay there during Christmas we can be even worse situation with all the fixtures and more injuries for sure and by the time you know it come 2026 we will be battling for relegation just like how Everton was last season and few seasons before that. It’s time to hit the panic button and as fans demand immediate response from the head coach and the players. If we get relegated only the fans will still be supporting this club even after relegation but the players and coaching staffs will leave to other clubs. So we have all the rights to demand for an immediate improvement.

author: @thibos.sefara
text:
What I've learned with LFC recent form is...
1. We don't use our opposition's strengths against them like low block defending, long throw-ins & set pieces... Open play is just not enough to win every single match & high ball posession doesn't necessarily lead to clean sheets nor goals if there's no inate desire to keep fighting for a win.

2. Mo Salah doesn't recognize his insane technical ability as of yet...Salah doesn't need to dribble pass 1,2,3 players to create some sort of a goal scoring chance like we're used to seeing rather with the type of ball posession we are capable of keeping we need to get Salah in position where he can thread those beautiful through balls past 3,4,5 player or his hard to defend crosses to the far post with his left foot on the right wing(this is where Florian can literally help him shine). He's still got it but, it's up to him to recognize that he can start looking up to find a better option in front of goal rather than taking a shot the moment he receives the ball. Haters gonna hate but Salah you're thee Egyptian King, & YNWA.❤🇮🇶👑

3. Virgil Van Dijk has been world class since he arrived at Anfield but his form lately has left us to face the hard truth that going forward, he either needs an extra center back in the back line for support or rather a natural defensive midfielder (I miss you Bajcetic, stunt on these haters when you come back stronger). Konaté on the other hand has been quite exceptional honestly is just that with the absense of Trent the responsibility of playing from the back has left him with mistakes that leave him highly criticized as a player forgetting what a Top class defender he is. Please by any means keep Konaté. Rather sell Gomez if the club signs Guehi.

4. Our team is full of ballers trust Slot we will eventually start clicking, we have like only Florian, Connor, Jeremy, Giovanni & Stefan unfortunately out on injury we have a high probability of signing a top class defender is Guehi. Its still scary. All these new signings are gonna ball.

5. Last but not least Slot is not the problem if anything he is the solution.
This is a man who won the Prem in his first season show respect where its worth.
In Slot Football I trust

Losing is disappointing but we stay together even through the tough times YNWA.❤

author: @NativeWorldTV
text:
The bigger issue at Liverpool FC right now isn’t about isolated moments or individuals it’s structural. There’s a visible lack of direction in how this team is being coached and set up. Patterns of play feel inconsistent, identity looks blurred, and the intensity that once defined Liverpool seems diluted.

Under Jürgen Klopp, dips in form happened but they felt like temporary setbacks within a clear philosophy. You always knew what Liverpool stood for. Now, under Arne Slot, there’s a growing concern that what we’re seeing isn’t just a blip it’s a decline without a clear roadmap back.

And that’s where the real frustration lies. Football fans can accept setbacks, even bad runs. What’s harder to accept is a lack of clarity, a drop in standards, and a sense that the team is drifting rather than evolving.

Because at the end of the day, a team is only ever as strong as the person leading it and right now, Liverpool don’t look like a side being led with the conviction, identity, and authority that once made them one of the most feared teams in Europe.

Every game it feels like you are watching flashes of good play but at this point, you can't even pretend to think there will be any end product. How can we play a 3 man (4when Wirtz tucked in) midfield and still look outnumbered. Jones for me, doesn't belong at this level sadly. We are missing legs, missing fight, missing an out ball. Missing teeth up top. Missing ball retention (Mama in net was smashing every ball back to city). Every time we had a throw in in our half it was more a question of if city would get a chance from it.
There is a lot wrong here this season and it's so difficult to single out one defect. Ultimately at that point, and I'm sad to say it because I advocate for giving slot at least until next January... But ultimately you have to look at the manager when so much is wrong.
If we got Guehi and Semenyo would we be in this position? Maybe not, but you can't think they'd have us that far ahead.

text: There's a lack of intent and urgency in some of the passing along the back line and midfield at times. Van Dijk, Konate and Mac Allister could pass to both flanks faster. Gakpo is not confident enough to take his fullback on the outside, so comes inside 90% of the time, which congests the middle of the pitch even more. Salah makes the wrong choice or executes his pass poorly far too often. The break away Salah led late on when he failed to find Szoboszlai's overlapping run with what should have been a simple pass to put him one on one with the GK was appallingly wasteful. The number of corners taken that didn't clear the first defender was also wasteful. Liverpool cannot miss out on CL next season just to accommodate Salah in the team. He scored against Wolves but 10 games without a PL goal says it all, he has to be dropped again now Frimpong is back. If Salah gets upset, tough, each player has to deliver week after week and he isn't anymore. He'll likely move on this summer anyway so the remainder of the season must look to the future, not massage the ego of a fantastic player who is sadly no longer at the required level.

author: @AaaBbb-dy8eg
text:
Let’s acknowledge that Arne Slot brought us the title last year, and I express my deep gratitude to him for that. But the fact that there is no clear style of play, and it’s unclear what we are trying to do with such a squad of players, is disappointing. Dominik Szoboszlai was pressing yesterday like a striker and constantly looking around for Hugo Ekitike. At times, two players press together leaving spaces open, and at other times no one presses at all — there is no understanding among the players, and that is the coach’s responsibility. It seems like he himself doesn’t fully know what system he wants to play.

Liverpool FC has never been a team that parks the bus. Before, there was always belief in a comeback during the match or even after it. I used to want stronger opponents to test ourselves against them — now there is only fear and hesitation. Thank you, Slot, but it needs to be said: it’s time to look for a new manager.

author: @blackheresy
text:
Arsenal fan here: Sacking Arne Slot right now would be reacting to symptoms, not the underlying problem. If the legs aren’t there, tactical adjustments tend to reduce damage, not create dominance. Klopp built physically dependent football—it required synchronized sprints, repeated pressing waves, and recovery runs. Once that physical edge drops, you can’t just “coach it back” in the middle of a congested season. There’s no training time, and fatigue compounds faster than ideas can be absorbed.

The midfield is more technical, less explosive & the distances between the players seem bigger, thus the press happens in moments, not waves. PSG are a difficult team because they have a rare combination of elite press resistant midfield with a deadly verticality. Slot had to deal with this tactically and with some sense of timidity. Newcastle pressed Barca well and still shipped 7 goals. Liverpool FC right now lack that synchronization: sometimes the front line presses but the midfield arrives a step late, and other times the midfield steps up while the back line holds a more cautious position. That disconnect creates gaps between units—exactly the kind of spaces a team like Paris Saint-Germain can play through with ease.

author: @luqld
text: Heart-broken to see my club fall down like this year, while witnessing the meteoric rise of the likes of PSG, Arsenal, Man City, etc. Football is like stock market which you cannot predict accurately. When FSG spent $400m on players, I believed everyone was extremely happy about it, believing that the owners heavily invested in the long-term future of the club and its sustained success; that's because they care so much about this club. As of now, everything is falling apart. I never believe that the owners are to blame. No sane person would want to invest their own money to get back, in today's dollars, less than what they have spent. Also, it is far easy to analyse a mistake after it has occurred, like saying what has gonr wrong at LFC in recruitment, management, and so on. Uncertainty is the key feature of a team sport like football. If things are easy enough like football pundits and thousands of fans of LFC have said, why did you all not bet your house and all savings on the outcome? In today's well developed financial markets, you have all tools available to make such bets. If you believe Slot is a bad manager, then why did you not place all your money at the beginning of the season that LFC would be falling down like this, so that the outcome as of now is like what you have predicted, and you would get huge profit? Team sport is far to predict with accuracy, with so many things going into the success of a team. One suddenly underperforming key player can kill the whole team. It's not a one/person sport like chess, tennis, F1 racing, where if you lose, it's only because you're weak, or you underperformed, and so on.

text:
Individually, the players are very talented, but what is ruining Liverpool is the lack of unity within the team. It feels like there are small groups forming among the players, almost like cliques, which is affecting team coordination and chemistry on the pitch. There is clearly a lack of innovation from the coach as well, and the tactical approach seems predictable and uninspiring.
Ekitike had a very poor performance and did not contribute much to the team. As for Salah, he is also a major factor in the team’s struggles. His play has become too predictable — he often just runs and shoots without bringing creativity or new ideas into the attack.
Wirtz, on the other hand, looks like a player from another planet with his exceptional talent and vision. However, it sometimes seems like his teammates are not on the same wavelength and even clash with him on the field, which prevents the team from benefiting fully from his brilliance.
